text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has warned that elements trying to impede the election process would be dealt with strictly.
- Pakistan Muslim League President Nawaz Sharif has vowed to shun the politics of revenge and vendetta and to make a new beginning, if voted to power in February 3 polls.
- With less than 24 hours left for curtains to draw on the election campaign, a lack of enthusiasm is seen in the port-city of Karachi, compared to other parts of southern Sindh province.
- Pakistan's caretaker government has abolished the 30-year-old state monopoly on the import of petroleum products.

- The U.S. has sent a clear message to politicians in Pakistan that if they do not get their act together, Washington would be willing to work comfortably with the army, even under a barely concealed military regime, analysts said.
- The Mohajir National Movement (MQM) has said that despite illegal and state enforced restrictions imposed on it, the party will contest the elections.
- The caretakers will leave behind them tough conditions for the future elected government to deal with the International Monetary Fund for securing uninterrupted funds.

- The final announcement of what has been declared a "consensus" award of the National Finance Commission for distribution of national resoruces among the provinces may be put off for at least a week or even after the February 3 elections.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The European Union has increased duty to 1.2 percent from 1.1 percent on leather imports from Pakistan since January 1, 1997.
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid has said the government was reviewing the energy policy and henceforth the emphasis should be on hydel power generation.
- The government has prepared as many as 250 cases of corruption against deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto and her jailed husband Asif Ali Zardari.
- World donors have proposed Pakistan to improve relations with India for the export of excess electrcity in the country through Rajasthan.
- The net inflow of portfolio investment by foreign fund houses during 1996 amounts to $46.685 million as against $9.350 million of 1995, registering a quantum jump of 80 percent.
- The Clinton administration has expressed the hope that the February 3 elections in Pakistan would be free and fair.
- The Southern Electric Power Company Ltd which has the financial assitance of the World Bank is likely to start its commercial production from December 28, 1997.
THE MUSLIM
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto has said she was being forced to accept the election results, whatever they may be, and sit on the opposition benches after February 3.
- The Swiss-based pre-shipment inspection company Societe Generale de Suveillance has said Pakistan government's decision to cancel its agreement was premature and breach of agreement.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
